# Saṁghabheda Sutta (Iti 18 (It 1.18 PTS It 10))

**ID:** Iti 18 (It 1.18 PTS It 10)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)

**Title (Pali):** Saṁghabheda Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Saṁghabheda Sutta* ("Schism in the Saṅgha", Iti 18) is a discourse in the *Ekakanipāta* of the *Itivuttaka*. The Buddha proclaims that causing a schism in the monastic community (*saṅgha*) brings about detriment, harm, and suffering for many beings, both human and divine. The prose discourse concludes with a verse warning that an instigator of schism (*saṅghabhedako*) falls into states of woe and hell, condemned to endure torment there for an entire aeon (*kappaṭṭho... kappam paccati*) [La Vallée Poussin 1988].

In the Chinese canon, a direct full parallel is found at T 765.9 (*僧破*). Passage-level parallels within the Pali canon include the *Paṭhamaānanda Sutta* (AN 10.39) and the *Saṁghabhedakakkhandhaka* of the Vinaya Khandhaka (Kd 17) [La Vallée Poussin 1988]. The verse concerning the schismatic's aeon-long suffering is prominent in later Abhidhamma debates, being cited and examined in the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 13.1, *Kappaṭṭhakathā*, and Kv 20.1, *Asañciccakathā*), where the views of the Rajagirika school are contested [La Vallée Poussin 1988]. DharmaNexus detects close textual reuse with Kv 20.1 (§3.1–3.6 aligned with §11.1–11.6) and with the sutta's direct thematic counterpart, the *Saṁghasāmaggī Sutta* (Iti 19, §0.1–4.1), alongside shared phrasing in the *Pañcakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 5) and formulaic openings common to other *Itivuttaka* texts [DharmaNexus].
